sources.note: Sec. 5.2 Phonology (pp.110-114: stops, nasals, laterals, rhotics, glides, vowels, clusters, word shape) says nothing about stress. The only remark is in sec. 5.1 p.110: 'Roth indicated stress, shown in the source by italics, here by underlining.' The wordlist (5.5, pp.120-133) therefore carries Roth's stress underlining (first syllable in the large majority of forms on p.120, e.g. kan-do, koo-pa, ka-ta, til-li, mung-a; non-initial in a few, e.g. nut-ti-na, to-lun-ya, u-ri-chi-mo) and Tindale's primes ('kanda, 'banjan, 'mana, 'talanja..), but no author states a rule. sources.citation: Roth, Walter E. 1897. Ethnological studies among the north-west-central Queensland Aborigines. Brisbane: Government Printer. (Cornell copy, archive.org cu31924029890328, scanned text)
sources.note: Ch. I sec. 3 (p.1) states that accentuation is expressed by printing the stressed syllable in italics (scanned garbled at that line); sec. 51 (p.43) says the comparative tables (pp.44-55, which include a 'Goa' column) are 'analysed into their component syllables, and accentuated and pronounced according to the basis laid down in section 3'. No rule of stress placement for Goa is stated; italics are lost in the scanned, so the marks are only recoverable from Blake & Breen's underlined reproduction.
Segment inventory only; nothing on stress or tone.
